label: draft, awaiting clinician review
note: Linked safety questions (contract v2). tier: hardStop = a 'Not sure' needs clarification; gateway = one opening question per topic, a 'Yes' or 'Not sure' opens its detail questions; weighted = adds points, 'Not sure' counts half; context = never asked by the safety check. askWhen: the question is asked when ANY clause matches (orUnknown also matches 'Not sure'). deniedValue: what this question counts as when the answers that would open it were given and did not open it (for example a gateway No, or a gradual onset for 'changed shape'). prefillFrom: an earlier app answer that already answers this question. Bank order is the asking order; a linked question waits until a question that opens it has been answered. fallback: a simpler, concrete question asked after a first 'Not sure' on a hard-stop question; its options give the canonical value. shortName: how a reason names the question.

questions.wording: Do you have chest pressure or tightness now?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Draft screening adaptation; referral policy requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: Chest pressure or tightness means a squeezing or heavy feeling in the chest. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: Does your chest feel heavy, tight or squeezed right now?

questions.wording: Are you struggling to breathe now?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Draft screening adaptation; referral policy requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: This means it is hard to catch your breath right now, even when resting. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: Can you say a full sentence without stopping for breath?

questions.wording: How did the pain start?

options.label: After an accident or injury, like a fall

questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Replaces the separate injury and sudden yes/no questions; filled from the basics answer when it was given. Draft adaptation, requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: Choose the option closest to how it began. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure.

questions.wording: Are you completely unable to move this arm?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Draft screening adaptation; referral policy requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: This asks whether the arm cannot move at all, not whether moving it hurts. Do not try a painful movement to answer. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: Can you lift your hand up to your mouth, even if it hurts?

questions.wording: Has the shoulder or arm changed shape?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Asked after an injury or a sudden start. Draft adaptation, requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: Look at both shoulders. A bump, a dip or an arm hanging differently counts. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: Is there a bump or a dip, or does the arm hang lower than the other side?

questions.wording: Do you have any unusual feeling in this arm or hand, such as numbness, pins and needles, or the arm feeling cold?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Opening question for the nerve and circulation topic. A No counts as No for its detail questions. Draft adaptation, requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: If you are not sure, choose Not sure and we will ask about each feeling separately.

questions.wording: Is there no feeling in any part of your arm or shoulder?
questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Draft screening adaptation; referral policy requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: This is about losing feeling, for example not feeling a light touch. Weakness is not the same. Do not test yourself. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: When your other hand touches the sore arm, does it feel the same as touching the good arm?

questions.wording: Do you have pins and needles in this arm?

options.label: Yes, but it comes and goes
Yes, and it does not go away

questions.label: draft, awaiting clinician review
questions.adaptation: Graded answer; only pins and needles that do not go away is an urgent sign. Draft adaptation, requires clinician review.
questions.clarification: Pins and needles that keep going or never fully settle count as not going away. If you cannot tell, choose Not sure again.

fallback.wording: Have you had pins and needles in this arm all day today?
